subject: Requesting extended prep runway & travel-aware slot for Finlytics evaluation
messages:
From: Megan Ortiz <megan.ortiz@finlytics.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-01T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Finlytics evaluation window

Hi Avery / Laura,

Thanks again for the time yesterday — Finlytics is excited to see Redwood run against our sample traces. We have two competing constraints on our side: our Head of Data (Samir) will be traveling the week of June 7, and our CTO may be at a board offsite the afternoon of June 4. Would you be able to run the evaluation on Friday June 4 at 9:00am PT or alternatively any time the following week? Ideally the slot includes a 30–45 minute dry run beforehand so we can confirm SSO and data access.

We can provide a small sample extract (CSV) and an initial set of prompts, but we may need one extra day for our security team to sign off on the sample export. Can you confirm what minimal artifacts you need from us to avoid a last-minute postponement?

Attaching a short list of expected deliverables on our side: sample_schema.csv (TBD), contact for SSO (megan.ortiz@finlytics.com), and a staging S3 path if needed.

Best,
Megan Ortiz
Product Ops, Finlytics

Attachments: sample_schema.csv (placeholder)

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Megan Ortiz <megan.ortiz@finlytics.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-01T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Finlytics evaluation window

Thanks Megan — great context. Short answer: we can be flexible, but given the things you mentioned we prefer to avoid single-day handoffs that leaves no room for prompt tuning, KV-cache priming, and SSO troubleshooting.

What we need from Finlytics before a live evaluation:
- Final sample export (<= 2000 rows) + sample_schema.csv
- Representative prompt set (we prefer JSONL for runs) — prompt_set_v3.jsonl works well
- Short list of success criteria (latency targets, throughput, example queries)
- SSO/ID provider test account or temporary credentials for the dry run

Proposal: move the live evaluation to Monday June 7 or Tuesday June 8 (mid-morning PT) and schedule a 30-minute dry run 24 hours earlier (so June 6 or 7 depending on final day). That gives us time to: ingest the sample, validate prompt outputs against your acceptance tests, and iterate on any guardrails.

If June 7–8 definitely conflicts with key stakeholders traveling, we can also consider a Friday (June 4) slot only if you can confirm the sample and prompt set by EOD June 2 and provide SSO access for the dry run. Otherwise we risk an immediate reschedule.

I'll loop in Laura for runbook/readiness and ask Rishi to validate the infra window for the requested dates.

Thanks — Avery
Avery Johnson
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference, inc.

Attachments referenced: prompt_set_v3.jsonl

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>, Megan Ortiz <megan.ortiz@finlytics.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-02T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Finlytics evaluation window

Looping in Rishi to confirm capacity. Quick operational checklist and compromise suggestion:

Checklist (Redwood needs):
- confirmed sample_schema.csv in CSV format (column names + types)
- prompt_set_v3.jsonl with at least 25 prompts for acceptance sampling
- dry-run account credentials (or SAML bypass test user)
- runbook review (we'll send dryrun_runbook_v1.pdf)

Compromise slot: we can do the live evaluation on Tuesday June 8 at 10:00am PT with a 30-minute dry run on Monday June 7 at 10:00am PT. That preserves a day to ingest and validate, while staying within your stated week. If your execs are traveling the week of June 7 and cannot attend, we can instead run the dry run June 6 and hold the live evaluation tentatively for June 10 — but we prefer the June 7/8 cadence.

Rishi — can you confirm GPU pool availability for 10:00am PT on June 8 and whether we need to lock capacity now? If there is contention we can offer a fallback model (gpt-quant-32) with slightly lower latency but deterministic throughput.

Megan — if you can upload sample_schema.csv and the prompt set to the Drive link I shared by EOD June 2, we'll lock the dry run on June 7. Otherwise we will default back to the Friday June 4 option only if everything is available by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

---
On Tue, Jun 1, 2027 at 5:03 PM Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai> wrote:

Attachments: dryrun_runbook_v1.pdf

From: Samir Kahn <sam.k@finlytics.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Megan Ortiz <megan.ortiz@finlytics.com>
Date: 2027-06-02T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Finlytics evaluation window

Thanks everyone — appreciate the pragmatic approach. We can't guarantee our Head of Data will be in-office June 7/8 (travel), so let's lock the dry run for June 6 at 10:00am PT and do the live evaluation on Monday June 10 at 10:00am PT. That ensures exec attendance and gives us room after travel to reconcile any follow-ups.

We'll upload a sanitized sample_schema.csv and the prompts to the shared Drive by EOD June 2 (Samir will confirm). Also, Megan will send a temporary test account for SSO; if there are any issues we can do a short recording of the login flow for debugging.

Please consider this confirmed unless you respond with a conflict by EOD June 2.

Thanks —
Samir Kahn
Head of Data, Finlytics
